💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:48, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 16:53.
  • Kocaelispor will be looking to extend their unbeaten run when they welcome Fenerbahce to Turka Arac Muayene Kocaeli Stadium on Saturday evening in the Turkish Super Lig.
  • Both teams are tied on 19 points from their opening 11 matches, with the hosts seventh in the table, one place below the visitors in sixth, although the Yellow Canaries have scored considerably more goals this season and therefore boast a significantly better goal difference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:48, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 16:53.

Kocaelispor will be looking to extend their unbeaten run when they welcome Fenerbahce to Turka Arac Muayene Kocaeli Stadium on Saturday evening in the Turkish Super Lig.

Both teams are tied on 19 points from their opening 11 matches, with the hosts seventh in the table, one place below the visitors in sixth, although the Yellow Canaries have scored considerably more goals this season and therefore boast a significantly better goal difference.

Kocaelispor have responded positively to consecutive defeats against Besiktas and Goztepe, going unbeaten in their last three league matches.

Their latest outing produced a 2-0 victory away to Eyupspor, following a goalless draw at home to Caykur Rizespor and a 2-1 victory over Alanyaspor, while they also recorded a 3-0 win over Mazidagi in the Turkish Cup during that run.

Selcuk Inan's side have built their season around a solid defensive foundation, with the hosts having conceded nine goals, a tally bettered only by Trabzonspor (8), giving them the second-best defence in the league, although the Gulf have scored the fewest goals among teams in the top half of the table (13).

Their home form has also been encouraging, with three victories, one draw and one defeat from five league matches at Kocaeli Stadium, where they have scored six goals and conceded just two, although they have failed to win either of their last two home fixtures (D1, L1).

However, Kocaelispor have struggled in this fixture over the years, failing to win any of their last 14 meetings with Fenerbahce, losing nine and drawing five, while they have also lost their last three home encounters.

Fenerbahce, meanwhile, arrive in Kocaeli after producing an emphatic response to their recent domestic setbacks, beating Corum 5-0 away from home in their last outing to return to winning ways.

The Yellow Canaries had previously suffered consecutive league defeats against Goztepe and Galatasaray, both by 2-1 scorelines, with the latter result particularly damaging as they fell further behind in the title race and prompted Ismail Kartal's resignation.

Emre Belozoglu subsequently took charge and has made an impressive start, recording a 3-2 victory over Liverpool in the Champions League before overseeing the emphatic win against Corum.

Fenerbahce's attack has been particularly productive this season, scoring 29 goals in 11 league matches to give them the most prolific frontline in the division, while their 10 goals conceded also represent the third-best defensive record, although they remain nine points off the top.

Kocaelispor are expected to be without Bruno Petkovic, who is dealing with a muscle injury, while Tanguy Zoukrou and Massadio Haidara are also doubtful with respective hamstring and tendon problems.

Aleksandar Jovanovic is another absentee, while Show is sidelined with an adductor injury, leaving Inan with decisions to make in midfield and defence.

Fenerbahce will be without Archie Brown, who is suspended, while Nathan Ake, Marco Asensio and Jayden Oosterwolde remain sidelined through injury.

Amara Diouf is also unavailable with a muscle problem, leaving Belozoglu without several options as he looks to maintain the momentum generated by the victory over Corum.

Kocaelispor possible starting lineup:.

Oztasdelen; Yildiz, Dijksteel, Ortakaya, Rivas; Bingol, Kutlu, Susoho; Agyei, Aye, Baku.

Fenerbahce possible starting lineup:.

Ederson; Semedo, Skriniar, Oppong, Mercan; Guendouzi, Yuksek; Greenwood, Kahveci, Aydin; Lukaku.

Kocaelispor have been considerably more reliable at home than away, conceding just twice in five league matches at their own stadium, but Fenerbahce's attacking record makes them difficult to overlook.

The hosts should be capable of making the contest competitive, particularly if they maintain their defensive discipline and exploit spaces on the counter-attack, but we expect the visitors' quality in the final third to ultimately prove decisive.

#26852. England deliver the spectacular as Three Lions strip world champions Spain of their invincibility and give Thomas Tuchel the proof that his coaching IS working, writes OLIVER HOLT

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1499 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

England deliver the spectacular as Three Lions strip world champions Spain of their invincibility and give Thomas Tuchel the proof that his coaching IS working, writes OLIVER HOLT

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1499 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:02 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 04:59 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • It has been revealed that thomas Tuchel had said he wanted evidence.
  • In a recent development, he needed a glimpse of his England team closing the gap to the best.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 17:02 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 04:59 EST, 16 November 2026.

It has been revealed that thomas Tuchel had said he wanted evidence. He needed to believe his coaching was working. He needed to see something that told him he could help England overcome those DNA deficiencies he had identified in the aftermath of the devastating World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.

In a recent development, he needed a glimpse of his England team closing the gap to the best. He needed to cling on to the idea that they could overhaul Spain, that the work he was doing could improve England so much they could win the European Championship in 2028 and end this country’s cursed cycle of despair.

It has been revealed that proof of concept, he called it on Saturday night when England arrived in Madrid. ‘This will be proof of concept on the highest level,’ Tuchel predicted. ‘It's the biggest test in world football. Spain seems unbeatable but we are trying to take it away from them. We are up for something spectacular.’.

Recent findings suggest that something spectacular is what Tuchel promised and something spectacular is what both he and England delivered. Spain had not lost for 43 matches, a world record, but number 44 was beyond them. For just over an hour, England destroyed them. They outplayed them. They stripped them of their invincibility.

And then, when Elliot Anderson was sent off after 63 minutes for pulling back Lamine Yamal, and Spain stormed back into the game, England somehow managed to hold on for a momentous victory in the screaming, yelling cauldron of the Metropolitano. This was proof alright. This was proof positive.

Sure, it was nervy for half an hour. And, yes, England nearly found a way to throw it away. But the way they played when it was 11 v 11 was enough for any England fan to believe that England under Tuchel can climb back to the summit of a major tournament and gaze down on a view they have not seen for 60 years.

England recorded a famous victory over Spain in Madrid as they won a five-goal thriller.

Elliot Anderson's red card opened the door for the world champions to mount a comeback.

James Trafford made a superb double save in stoppage time to preserve England's lead.

It has been revealed that yes, this was a Nations League dead rubber because both teams were already guaranteed progress to the quarter-finals next March, but there was no mistaking its wider significance. This was proof England are good enough to turn away from the trail of tears that has been their path for so long. Before the game, Spain had held the World Cup aloft again as one final reminder of England’s failure but by the end, by the time goalkeeper James Trafford had added to the drama with a miraculous double save, the glory and the 3-2 triumph was England’s.

Industry observers note that spain had won their last 12 matches in succession and the sport’s last two major tournament. They had not been beaten since March 2024 and had not lost at home since September 2022. England ended that run with 10 men. What a night. It was a special kind of crazy.

England had celebrated Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph and caps record at Wembley last week but Spain took things a stage further before the game. The boys who won the U15 World Cup were introduced to the crowd. Then the World Cup itself was carried on for goalkeeper Unai Simon to hold aloft.

England ignored it all. They started the game like an express train. They nearly took the lead inside the first two minutes when Jude Bellingham met a corner from Declan Rice on the edge of the six-yard-box and was only denied by a brilliant reaction save from Simon. Gordon’s follow-up was destined for the bottom corner before it was blocked by a Spain defender.

It has been revealed that spain were rattled. The crowd whistled. England forced their opponents into mistake after mistake at the back. From one of those successful presses, Kane drilled a shot inches wide. Gordon, who has made such a fine start to his Barcelona career, revelled on the stage and caused right back Marc Pubill all manner of anxieties.

Recent findings suggest that spain could barely break out of their own half but when they did, after a quarter of an hour, Yamal ran at Lewis Hall and nutmegged him before Rice chopped the teenager down. Rice was booked by French referee Clement Turpin and Lamal windmilled his hands in the air to wind up the crowd.

Industry observers note that pubill was replaced midway through the half. It looked like an injury but it could have been hurt pride or twisted blood. Gordon had barely given him a moment’s rest. In fact, Gordon was tireless. He harried Martin Zubimendi off the ball with ease and almost set up a chance for Bellingham.

England got the goal they deserved a minute before half-time. The build-up was controversial. Anderson played a fine through ball to Kane that doubled as a crunching tackle on Marc Cucurella. Cucurella went down as if he had been shot, which is what Cucurella always does.

Ben White slotted the ball through the keeper's legs after a brilliant England move.

Harry Kane celebrates goal No 93 for England after giving them the lead from the penalty spot.

Industry observers note that the referee allowed play to continue. Kane advanced on goal and turned inside Pau Cubarsi, Spain’s brilliant young defender. Cubarsi brought him down and the referee pointed to the spot. Cucurella still lay prone. Bellingham, his Real Madrid teammate, leaned over him and told him what he thought of him.

Sources indicate that there were a whole host of VAR checks but England passed all of them. The crowd whistled their distaste. Kane missed a penalty in the Wembley game between these two teams in September but he did not miss this one. Simon guessed the right way but Kane hit it too fiercely and it bulged the back of the net. It was his 93rd goal for England.

Spain are not used to being bossed around like this. Tempers flared after the whistle blew for half-time. Ben White and Fabian Ruiz joined in a disagreement of some sort and soon there was a flurry of pushing and shoving. It stopped short of being a melee but it was obvious Spain were shaken.

According to recent reports, eight minutes into the second half, England went further ahead. Rice swung a corner into the centre of the box and, as the usual wrestling match unfolded, Ezri Konsa ran in gloriously unmarked and nodded the ball down and past the helpless Simon from close range.

Sources indicate that four minutes later, against a general backdrop of disbelief, England were three ahead. What a goal it was, too. Bellingham, who had been his usual superhuman self, muscled his way free in the centre and fed the ball out to Kane.

It has been revealed that kane held the ball up and played it back to Bellingham on the edge of the box. Bellingham spotted the overlapping run of White and found him with a clever pass. White took a touch and slotted the ball past Simon. It was the Arsenal full-back’s first competitive England start, too. Maybe now England fans will stop booing him.

This was the night Thomas Tuchel had been crying out for as he got the evidence he demanded.

Ezri Konsa met Declan Rice's set-piece to plant an unstoppable header in the back of the net.

Recent findings suggest that but then, midway through the half, England gave Spain a lifeline. Jarell Quansah was caught in possession by Yamal and as Yamal bore down on goal, Anderson pulled him back. Anderson was shown a red card and Spain were awarded a penalty. Oyarzabal waited for Trafford to commit himself and then stroked the ball into the opposite corner.

Recent findings suggest that the atmosphere in the stadium was transformed. Spain sensed vulnerability in England for the first time. Fifteen minutes from time, they pulled another goal back. Yamal sprinted away down the right and slid the ball into the middle for substitute Nico Williams, who sidefooted it past Trafford.

According to recent reports, now, it was like the Alamo. Yamal tormented England. Trafford dived at full length to push away one of his shots and then got down at his near post to divert a shot that was creeping in. White produced another of the moments of the night with a flying block to keep out a goalbound shot from Williams.

Spain threw everything at England but England would not yield. When Trafford made that double save, everyone knew. It was to be England’s night. Tuchel had his proof of concept.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, southampton stuck by head coach Tonda Eckert after the Spygate saga.
  • Sources indicate that now, the club have confirmed that Eckert’s new deal at St Mary’s is done.
  • Sources indicate that eckert was appointed as the Saints’ permanent boss in December 2025 after an impressive spell as caretaker after Will Still’s sacking.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, southampton stuck by head coach Tonda Eckert after the Spygate saga. And, when his punishment of a suspended ban and fine was confirmed, it soon emerged that the Saints were preparing a latest contract offer to secure the boss’ future beyond the end of the 2026/27 campaign.

Sources indicate that now, the club have confirmed that Eckert’s new deal at St Mary’s is done. His new contract will run until 2029, marking a two-year extension on his existing terms.

Sources indicate that eckert was appointed as the Saints’ permanent boss in December 2025 after an impressive spell as caretaker after Will Still’s sacking. The 33-year-old had only joined as U21s head coach in the summer, but his quick ascent has seen him emerge as one of Europe’s brightest coaching prospects.

Eckert’s breakthrough has been mightily impressive, despite the fact Spygate still casts a cloud over his Southampton record.

Industry observers note that after a string of roles in Germany and assistant manager positions at Barnsley and Genoa, Eckert’s step to become the Saints’ U21s boss was a good one for the trajectory of his career. Few saw him making such an early rise into the first-team role, but Still’s struggles and his success as caretaker meant he was promptly solidified in his place as boss.

He has averaged just under two points per game in his time as permanent head coach, and the four-point deduction his side started the season with is a thing of the past. That and a new contract for Eckert has helped lead the turmoil of Spygate in the past.

Importantly though, Eckert’s fresh deal will fend off potential admirers. Clubs were bound to have him on the radar as he closed on the end of his contract, but a hefty compensation fee will now have to be paid to prise him away from the South Coast club.

Sources indicate that spygate will be brought up at every corner by opposing fans and it will have a place in English football history forever. Eckert will face questions about it for the foreseeable, and many will still debate that the punishment he faced was not strong enough.

Sources indicate that however, Eckert and the Saints are moving on by focusing on the long term and delivering success on the pitch. A new contract solidifies the club’s commitment to him despite the end to last season.

After losing 1-0 to Preston North End before the break, Eckert will be eager to see his side respond when they face Derby County this Saturday.

Industry News: Spurs finally score... but still lose

📅 16 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (5021 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.
  • It could have been something different.
  • Industry observers note that “I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

They scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

It could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, showed this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

Industry observers note that “I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

In a recent development, THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6.

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

Recent findings suggest that yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

Recent findings suggest that “We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”.

According to recent reports, rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

According to recent reports, big save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku.

According to recent reports, the miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

In a recent development, for all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

“I see him training every day,” Iraola mentioned. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he demonstrates is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”.

Simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

According to recent reports, is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a new contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

Industry observers note that “I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola mentioned. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

It has been revealed that “But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no complications. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”.

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi mentioned. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”.

Sources indicate that tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:48.
  • Genclerbirligi will be looking to return to winning ways when they welcome Gaziantep to Eryaman Stadium on Saturday afternoon in the Turkish Super Lig.
  • The hosts sit 14th in the table with 11 points from as many matches, three points clear of the relegation zone, while the visitors are 16th and in the drop zone with eight points after losing seven of their opening 11 league fixtures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:48.

Genclerbirligi will be looking to return to winning ways when they welcome Gaziantep to Eryaman Stadium on Saturday afternoon in the Turkish Super Lig.

The hosts sit 14th in the table with 11 points from as many matches, three points clear of the relegation zone, while the visitors are 16th and in the drop zone with eight points after losing seven of their opening 11 league fixtures.

Genclerbirligi head into Saturday's encounter after suffering a 3-0 defeat away to Besiktas in their last league outing, having been unable to build on the confidence gained from their emphatic 5-0 victory over Alanyaspor a week earlier.

That win was their biggest of the campaign and followed another 5-0 success against Karakopru Belediyespor in the Turkish Cup, but their return to league action in Istanbul brought them back down to earth as Besiktas scored twice before half-time and added a third after the break.

The Red-and-Blacks have now lost three of their last four league matches and won just one of their last nine, with their only victory during that period coming against Alanyaspor, while they have conceded 21 goals in 11 league fixtures, the third-highest total in the division.

Their defensive record has been a particular concern away from home, where they have conceded 14 times in five matches and scored just once, although their performances in Ankara have generally been more encouraging.

Genclerbirligi have collected eight points from six home league matches, winning twice, drawing twice and losing twice, and they have scored nine goals at Eryaman Stadium in the competition, with their 2-1 victory over Fenerbahce representing the highlight.

Bernd Storck's side will hope to avoid another winless streak by bouncing back immediately, with optimism stemming from their home results and the fact that they beat the visitors on this ground in their last meeting here, while they have also never lost to them at home (W4, D1).

Gaziantep, meanwhile, have endured a much more difficult spell, losing their last six league matches and failing to score in each of their most recent two outings.

Their latest defeat came at home against Kasimpasa, who secured a 2-0 victory with both goals coming before the break, while they had previously lost by the same scoreline away to Trabzonspor.

Those results followed defeats against Erzurumspor, Istanbul Basaksehir, Corum and Kocaelispor, leaving the Red-and-Blacks with just two wins and two draws from their opening 11 matches, alongside seven defeats.

The club subsequently parted tech giant with coach Orhan Ak by mutual agreement following the loss to Kasimpasa, leaving Gaziantep to prepare for this fixture amid another managerial change.

Assistant coach Mustafa Aksoy oversaw the first training session after Ak's departure, but Volkan Demirel has been appointed as their new head coach, and the club will be hoping that a change in the dugout can bring an immediate response.

Genclerbirligi Turkish Super Lig form:.

Industry News: Sergio Navarro’s style and the key individuals: Milan Futuro tactical analysis

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Milan Futuro decided to go in a new direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?
  • Milan debuted the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Milan Futuro decided to go in a new direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?

Milan debuted the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season. with the aim of creating a pathway for academy players to break into the first team. The project was designed to bridge the physical and technical gap between the Primavera and senior football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, things didn’t go well in year one, as Daniele Bonera didn’t see out the season as the head coach. He recently stated he didn’t think the squad was ready for the level, and ultimately Massimo Oddo was unable to save the team from relegation to Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football.

Industry observers note that with promotion back to Serie C the objective, this summer the Rossoneri turned to Sergio Navarro, a coach with good pedigree in Spain. The Futuro now appear to have a clearer structure, a defined playing identity and the right guidance, as Rohit Rajeev has outlined.

Industry observers note that under Barquero, Milan Futuro operate in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Asanji leads the line, with Ossola playing as the number 10 and Vos and Guernier occupying the wide positions.

Plazotta and Pandolfi form the double pivot, while Cisse and Pagliei partner at centre-back, with Perera and Colombo completing the back four.

Industry observers note that milan Futuro favour a possession-oriented approach, circulating the ball patiently at a measured tempo while waiting for gaps to emerge in the opposition’s defensive structure. They also use passing triangles effectively to create short passing options and play through the opposition’s high press.

In possession, Milan Futuro adopt a 3-1-6 structure, with Barquero showing little hesitation in committing players forward to create numerical overloads in the opposition half.

Industry observers note that asanji positions himself just behind the opposition’s defensive line, keeping the centre-backs occupied and preventing them from stepping forward freely. Meanwhile, Pandolfi and Plazotta maintain parallel positions in the double pivot, providing a stable base for the attacking structure.

In the opposition half, Milan Futuro keep the distances between players very short, allowing them to combine through quick, one-touch passes.

This also helps them create ball-sided overloads, with two or three players surrounding the Milan player in possession to provide close passing options. Once they enter the opposition half, the tempo increases as Milan look to become more direct and progress towards goal.

Similar to Amorim’s approach at Sporting, Milan Futuro form vertical corridors with three players positioned one behind another. This structure facilitates quick passing combinations while also creating movement to manipulate the opposition.

When Milan players drop to form these corridors or create overloads, they often drag defenders with them, opening spaces elsewhere to exploit.

It has been revealed that milan Futuro look to press the opposition high up the pitch, adopting a 4-4-2 shape with a man-oriented pressing scheme. This allows them to put pressure on the opposition’s build-up and restrict the time and space available to play out from the back.

Milan Futuro also set up pressing traps by deliberately leaving the opposition’s wide player unmarked. The pass towards the wide player acts as the pressing trigger, prompting Milan’s players to jump out of their positions and aggressively close down the receiver, while cutting off the available passing options.

Milan Futuro maintain an extremely narrow defensive shape, prioritising the protection of central spaces and forcing the opposition towards the flanks.

Once the opposition attempts to progress through the wide areas, the press shifts across to create numerical overloads around the ball, while Guernier and Colombo provide cover and prevent the opposition from switching play to the opposite flank.

Perhaps the most important aspect of Barquero’s approach is his willingness to build the system around his players’ strengths and allow them the freedom to express themselves.

According to recent reports, rather than focusing solely on tactical adaptability, he appears equally committed to their individual development and helping them grow as footballers. Here are a few examples.

In a recent development, one of Milan Futuro’s methods of chance creation is to play direct passes into Asanji. His ability to position himself between the ball and the opposition defender, using his physicality to shield possession and hold up play, is crucial to this approach.

Rather than asking him to adapt to the role of a more technically oriented, ball-playing striker, Barquero has built a mechanism that makes the most of his existing strengths.

According to recent reports, perhaps the clearest demonstration of Barquero’s coaching ability is his utilisation of Vos and Guernier. Guernier is a natural winger/forward, while Vos is more accustomed to playing as an attacking midfielder.

Within the 3-1-6 structure, Vos often inverts from the left flank into an inside-left role, allowing Perera to provide the width.

In a recent development, at times, he is also given the freedom to interchange positions with Plazotta, allowing him to drop into midfield or advance further up the pitch. This positional freedom helps him develop his midfield qualities and realise his potential.

Guernier, meanwhile, tends to maintain his width, stretching the opposition’s defensive line and creating space for Vos and the other attackers to exploit.

Barquero also gives Guernier the freedom to take on his direct opponent, even when he is outnumbered, allowing him to use his dribbling ability without being restricted by the team’s structure.

Ossola, who is particularly effective at receiving between the lines and turning with the ball, is allowed to operate higher up the pitch, closer to the opposition’s defensive line.

Idrissi, on the other hand, prefers to receive possession deeper, where he can dictate play with his passing range or carry the ball forward through dribbling.

  • Galatasaray will aim to stretch their lead at the top of the Turkish Super Lig table when they host struggling Samsunspor on Saturday afternoon.
  • The match has been moved from RAMS Park because of pitch problems and will now be played at Basaksehir Fatih Terim Stadium, with the league leaders given extra time to carry out maintenance and improvement work ahead of their upcoming UEFA Champions League fixture against Aston Villa.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:49, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:30.

Galatasaray will aim to stretch their lead at the top of the Turkish Super Lig table when they host struggling Samsunspor on Saturday afternoon.

The match has been moved from RAMS Park because of pitch problems and will now be played at Basaksehir Fatih Terim Stadium, with the league leaders given extra time to carry out maintenance and improvement work ahead of their upcoming UEFA Champions League fixture against Aston Villa.

Galatasaray went into the international break on a six-game winning streak in all competitions, a run that began with a 1-0 victory over Genclerbirligi before they beat Lille 4-2 in the Champions League and Fenerbahce 2-1 at home in the league.

The Lions then won 4-0 away to Konyaspor, beat Stuttgart 2-0 in the Champions League and edged Amedspor 4-3 just before the break, with their attacking output particularly impressive as they scored at least twice in five of those six matches.

In the victory over Amed, Galatasaray raced into a 3-0 lead through Rafael Leao's early strike, an own goal from goalkeeper Alban Lafont and Alexey Batrakov's effort before the hour mark, but they subsequently conceded twice before Baris Alper Yilmaz restored their two-goal cushion in the 80th minute, only for the hosts to concede again in stoppage time before holding on for the victory.

Okan Buruk's side have suffered just one league defeat this season, a 4-0 loss away to Trabzonspor, which has left them with 28 points from 11 matches, having also drawn 2-2 at home against Corum in their opening game of the campaign.

Keeping opponents off the scoresheet at home has been an concern for Cimbom, who have conceded in five of their six home league matches this season, including each of their last three.

Samsunspor won the last meeting against Galatasaray to end a nine-game losing streak in this fixture, but the visitors arrive in considerably worse form this season.

However, they received a much-needed boost just before the break, beating Konyaspor 1-0 at home to end an eight-game winless streak, which had been a club record.

It was also the first victory under Nenad Bjelica, who was appointed in October to replace Thorsten Fink, who was dismissed after nine months in charge following just one win in his opening seven matches.

Samsunspor are 17th on seven points, one place above the bottom and one point from safety, and while they finally recorded some positivity before the break, they travel to a venue where they have lost eight consecutive games, leaving them with a difficult task after the international hiatus.

Galatasaray Turkish Super Lig form:.

Galatasaray form (all competitions):.

Samsunspor Turkish Super Lig form:.

Galatasaray have major absentees, with Victor Osimhen undergoing surgery on a loose fragment in his left knee after the Stuttgart game and expected to be out for several weeks.

Leao is also sidelined through injury, while goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir picked up a shoulder problem on international duty and is not expected to play, with Gunay Guvenc tipped to start between the posts.

Davinson Sanchez is also unavailable after withdrawing from Colombia's squad with a muscle problem, while Roland Sallai is sidelined through injury and Batrakov is also listed as unavailable.

Samsunspor have fewer concerns, although Celil Yuksel is sidelined through injury and Fatih Kaya remains a doubt.

Mohamed Bayo is expected to lead the attack, with Tanguy Coulibaly, Oskar Ohlenschlæger and Afonso Sousa providing support from the attacking midfield positions.

Galatasaray possible starting lineup:.

Gunay; Singo, Bardakci, Jakobs, Elmali; Torreira, Lemina; Akgun, Sara, Sane; Yilmaz.

Samsunspor possible starting lineup:.

Bayazit; Mendes, Erakovic, Drapinski, Tomasson; Watt, Onur; Coulibaly, Ohlenschlæger, Sousa; Bayo.

Galatasaray are without their main striker, first-choice goalkeeper and Leao, but they still possess considerably greater squad depth and arrive in strong form, which should prove too much for Samsunspor as we expect the league leaders to secure a comfortable victory.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:07, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:12.
  • Still unbeaten in Serie A this season, free-scoring Roma will return to action with a trip to lowly Parma on Saturday evening.
  • Sitting third - just behind reigning champions Inter Milan and city rivals Lazio - the Giallorossi averaged four goals per game as they posted three consecutive league wins before the break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:07, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:12.

Still unbeaten in Serie A this season, free-scoring Roma will return to action with a trip to lowly Parma on Saturday evening.

Sitting third - just behind reigning champions Inter Milan and city rivals Lazio - the Giallorossi averaged four goals per game as they posted three consecutive league wins before the break.

Despite suffering two agonising Champions League defeats in recent weeks, Roma have hardly faltered on the domestic front; they are one of only two teams still undefeated in Serie A, alongside surprise leaders Lazio.

Soon after swatting Cagliari and Udinese aside, the Giallorossi signed off for the international period with a comfortable 3-0 home victory over Sassuolo, in which rising star Rodrigo Mora scored for a third straight league game.

It was an increasingly rare clean sheet for a club boasting the most lethal attack in Italy's top flight: Roma are only the fourth team in 65 years to hit the 30-goal mark by Serie A’s 11th matchday.

Dating back to last term, Gian Piero Gasperini’s side have scored at least twice in all but one of their last 16 league fixtures, only failing to do so in Como, where Donyell Malen was sent off.

Allowed to roam freely into the opposition area, defenders have collectively contributed eight goals this season, easing any pressure on Malen, Mora and their fellow forwards.

Beginning the build-up to next month’s Derby della Capitale, Roma will now seek a fifth straight win over Parma, who they beat 3-2 on their most recent trip to Stadio Tardini, with Malen inevitably scoring twice.

In fact, Parma have lost 13 of the past 20 league meetings on home turf, so history will not be on their side this weekend.

The hosts have endured a rocky start to the season, already changing coaches, and upcoming boss Alberto Gilardino only celebrated his first victory shortly before the break.

However, days after stunning Atalanta with a shock 3-0 win in Bergamo, his side were beaten by Bologna in the Derby dell'Emilia.

Parma were reduced to 10 men within eight minutes at the Tardini, after Abdoulaye Ndiaye was dismissed following a VAR review, and they ultimately ended up losing 2-1.

As a result, the Gialloblu sit just one point above the bottom three, with only eight points on the board so far.

The club’s second-highest Serie A scorer during his playing days, Gilardino has a more modest managerial record, and he surely faces another survival scrap after last term’s fruitless fight with Pisa.

Roma have welcomed Paulo Dybala and first-choice goalkeeper Mile Svilar back during the break, but the latter’s deputy Pierluigi Gollini remains a doubt after missing two games with a back injury.

Devyne Rensch (adductor) and Lorenzo Pellegrini (thigh) are still sidelined, but Gasperini should have everyone else available.

A sure starter up front, Malen sits joint-second in the Capocannoniere rankings with eight Serie A goals, and the Dutch striker also scored for his country in the UEFA Nations League last week.

Meanwhile, Parma will be missing Argentine forward David Romero, who sustained a serious shoulder injury against Bologna.

Diego Carlos is also struggling with a thigh strain, injury-prone midfielder Adrian Bernabe is a significant doubt, and Ndiaye must serve a one-match ban.

In the absence of Romero, teenage starlet Simone Lontani could partner El Bilal Toure, but Nesta Elphege is another contender.

Parma possible starting lineup:.

Daffara; Delprato, Troilo, Drobnic; Britschgi, Fabbian, Sierro, Keita, Valeri; Lontani, Toure.

Svilar; Mancini, Ndicka, Hermoso; Molina, Cristante, Kone, Wesley; Soule, Mora; Malen.

Roma can pick up where they left off before the break, as a limited Parma side will struggle to match their intensity and flair.

A fourth straight win in Serie A will warm the Giallorossi up for next week's tough trip to Paris Saint-Germain.

Industry observers note that bolton Wanderers return from the international break looking to pick themselves up from a demoralising defeat to Derby County two weeks ago. Steven Schumacher’s team sit seven points above the bottom three but risk sliding at pace if they can’t begin to fix their defensive woes, having conceded 29 goals so far.

The biggest glitch for the Trotters is their home form. BWFC have lost all but two of seven games at the Toughsheet Community Stadium, conceding 15 of their 29 goals at the ground. Wanderers have to find form at home, and will hope Saturday’s game can be the start.

Sources indicate that whilst Bolton Wanderers have been trending down, it is the opposite for Portsmouth. Despite losing 2-1 to Stoke City before the break, Pompey have won three of their last six, sitting just two points off the top eight.

John Mousinho’s side head to Bolton with a good record against their opponents and will be hopeful of returning to winning ways at 15:00 on Saturday.

Bolton Wanderers have welcomed back all four internationals without any injury concern.

Thierry Gale and Chris Forino, who faced each other whilst playing for Barbados and Saint Lucia, both came back unscathed. The same can be noted for Gaizka Larrazabal and Josh Sheehan, who both played one game for their respective nations.

Eoin Toal and Gavin Bazunu could be available on Saturday after training this week.

In a recent development, bazunu in particular could be a massive boost for BWFC. Whilst Jack Bonham has proven to be a solid deputy, the Irishman has been an astute signing from Southampton, preventing 1.45 expected goals and claiming two clean sheets this season.

Elsewhere John McAtee, Ryan Hardie, Jayden Nelson and Ethan Erhahon all remain out injured.

Bonham; Stephenson, Forino, Davies, Famewo; Sheehan, Simons; Larrazabal, Rodrigues, Gale; Dalby.

With Bazunu’s full status as of yet unconfirmed, Bonham keeps his place, but the defence is reshuffled. Akin Famewo moves to left-back in place of Max Conway, with Ben Davies taking his position in central defence.

Recent findings suggest that bolton Wanderers have need to stop conceding easy goals and they have performed better playing one central defender on either side of the back four. Famewo has done so before and played well. On Saturday, he will have the task of handling Adrian Segecic and Terry Devlin on the Pompey right.

Gaizka Larrazabal continues at right-wing having been one of Wanderers’ better players at Pride Park, whilst Gale also keeps his place, simply because he is one of the only wide men who often tracks back, something BWFC need to stop their defensive concerns.

Bolton Wanderers’ clash with Portsmouth kicks off at 15:00 on Saturday afternoon.

It has been a positive international break for Diego Moreira, who continued his excellent form from club football.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write this morning, Ruben Amorim will welcome Moreira back to Milanello soon. The winger has become a regular starter and producing goals and assists, but the Portuguese coach knows the pitfalls of the match against Frosinone all too well.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that therefore, starting Thursday – when the squad will be fully back together after the day off tomorrow – everyone’s minds will be focused solely on the new busy schedule awaiting the Rossoneri until Christmas. More specifically, seven matches from Sunday until December 19th.

Immediately after the last international break, the Rossoneri drew away to Sassuolo, a result that certainly wasn’t greeted with a smile. The goal is to avoid repeating that misstep against Alvini’s team, and Moreira will be key to that.

According to recent reports, despite his 22 years of age and the €50m valuation plus bonuses that could have weighed heavily on his shoulders, Diego hasn’t taken long to win over Milan fans. In his last six league matches (he missed two due to injury), he’s scored four goals and provided three assists.

He has also demonstrated his ability to switch roles with ease, playing as a winger on the right or left, as a wing-back or even as a full-back. He plays with the boldness of someone who targets his opponent and tries to dribble past him, something that fans always appreciate.

Moreira always seeks one-on-one situations, both due to his strengths and the explicit request of Amorim, who asks his wide players to create numerical superiority. Diego is succeeding remarkably, as his assist for Christian Pulisic in the derby indicates, as he got past Carlo Augusto and crossed.

Moreira made the difference against Italy on Sunday too: not only did he score the fourth goal, which he celebrated by making a gesture of ‘one, two, three and four’ with his fingers, but he also kept accelerating, hit the woodwork, shot wide once more and had two shots blocked by his opponents.

In a recent development, he set up De Bruyne for a shot, had more touches than anyone else in the opponents’ area (11) and often took on Calafiori and Dimarco, delighting the crowd with a spectacular backheel. He had around 50 touches and 27/31 completed passes, earning the applause of the entire stadium when he came off.

Moreira is currently captivating thanks to his drive and desire. He’s that way at Milan and he’s that way with the national team. That’s why there’s a version of the Rossoneri with him and another without him which, frankly, isn’t as threatening.

Amorim carefully integrated him into the team’s operations at the start of the season, but now he has broken the padlock off and now considers him a key player in the team. This doesn’t mean he won’t need a breather, given the schedule, but the coach will have to think about the right moments to rest.

With four goals in Serie A (one every 121 minutes), he’s already matched his four goals from last season in Ligue 1, and he has no intention of stopping. He feels the confidence in himself and the team.

It has been revealed that the leap from Ligue 1 to Serie A didn’t bother him. In fact, he intends to continue dancing on the pitch, just like in the derby or against Italy. On Sunday, he wants to show he has the same energy with which he brought Italy to its knees. Milan and San Siro await him.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and WILL GOVE.

Published: 07:00 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EST, 16 November 2026.

Amar Dedic might have fancied himself as Robin Hood – but the Newcastle United defender's latest adventure in the Northumberland countryside led to a rather less merry altercation with police last week.

The Magpies star sparked a major police operation after being spotted carrying a bow and arrows near a reservoir outside Newcastle, with at least six patrol cars joining the search for the £30million player.

After tracking down and questioning the Bosnian, officers were satisfied there was no threat to the public and that the equipment was intended for recreational use.

But Dedic's escapade was certainly not the first time a footballer has found himself in hot water over the possession, carrying or use of a weapon, with brass knuckles, meat cleavers and BB guns among the bizarre arsenal of items to have attracted the authorities' attention over the years.

Marcus Bent, with a meat cleaver, in Surrey.

Former Middlesbrough and Everton forward Marcus Bent was tasered in his own home by police after threatening armed police officers with a meat cleaver and kitchen knife while under the influence of cocaine.

Bent, who avoided jail in 2016 after he pleaded guilty to possession of cocaine and affray, called Surrey Police after thinking he had discovered an intruder in his home.

Recent findings suggest that officers arrived at the scene but were initially unable to gain access to the property. Guildford Crown Court heard how the officers were about to use a battering ram to gain entry when a bare-chested Bent 'flung' open the door holding two chef's knives, with his 'eyes wide, jaw clenched and his body rigid'.

It has been revealed that bent, who was handed a 12-month sentence, suspended for two years, later said: 'I was paranoid and I was hallucinating. I felt there were people in my house. I remember thinking the door handle was moving.

Recent findings suggest that 'At no point was I ever going to take someone's life. I called them because I was hallucinating, paranoid, terrified.'.

Marcus Bent arrives at court before pleading guilty to possession of cocaine and affray.

Ashley Cole, with an air rifle, in Cobham.

To most, Ashley Cole is England's all-time greatest full-back but the three-time Premier League winner also made headlines for an infamous training ground air rifle incident.

Back in 2011 while playing for Chelsea, Ashley Cole accidentally shot and injured 21-year-old student Tom Cowan, who was on work experience at the Blues' training ground in Cobham, Surrey.

The Champions League winning left-back was reportedly 'larking about' with a .22 air rifle and accidentally shot Cowan from just five feet away.

The student had assumed he would get an invaluable experience on his brief visit to Cobham but instead had to be treated by medics and rest for the remainder of the day after the shot was fired.

Cole accidentally shot a 21-year-old on work experience at Chelsea's training ground.

Darren Bent, with a BB Gun, in Kesgrave.

Ex-England star Darren Bent ran into trouble early in his career when he was questioned over the alleged shooting of a 12-year-old boy with a ball-bearing gun.

While starring for his boyhood club Ipswich at the age of 20 in May 2004, Bent was arrested on suspicion of possession of an imitation firearm with intent to cause violence, before he was placed on bail and eventually released without charge pending further investigations.

According to a Suffolk Police statement at the time, a 12-year-old boy at a play area in Kesgrave had been struck in the back by a pellet from a ball-bearing gun (BB Gun). The incident was reported to authorities by his mother.

Bent, who was given a formal caution for his actions, went on to enjoy a fruitful career in the Premier League, representing the likes of Charlton, Tottenham, Sunderland and Aston Villa while also winning 13 caps for the Three Lions.

Early on his career Premier League legend Darren Bent was arrested on suspicion of possession of an imitation firearm.

Karim Adeyemi, with brass knuckles, in Germany.

The only member of this list to still be playing is Germany and Barcelona's Karim Adeyemi who was fined £396,000 in 2025 for possessing a pair of brass knuckles.

The former Borussia Dortmund forward was caught with the knuckles back in 2024, at the age of 22, but had to wait until the following year to receive his punishment.

Under German law the possession, procurement and use of brass knuckles is prohibited. The young winger avoided a public trial and a criminal record and was given a fine consisting of 60 daily payments of £6,600.

Although he never used the weapon, the German was in hot water  as he briefly lost his starting place in the German national team and at Borussia Dortmund.

The Westphalia giants released a statement saying: 'BVB always takes criminal allegations seriously and uses them as an opportunity to discuss them with its employees while respecting confidentiality obligations.'.

Adeyemi was lucky to dodge prison time after being charged with the possession of brass knuckles.

Diego Maradona, with an air rifle, in Buenos Aires.

Argentina icon Diego Maradona caused injuries to four people when he fired an air rifle at journalists and photographers while hiding behind a parked Mercedes outside his Buenos Aires home in February 1994.

Four years later, Maradona was found guilty of assault with a weapon and given a suspended prison sentence of two years and ten months, which was later reduced to an even two years.

To many he is the best of all time but Diego Maradona is hardly infallible off the pitch.

Despite appealing against the sentence which they claimed was 'too light', the journalists injured by Maradona said the verdict at least demonstrated there was 'justice for all' in Argentina.

'At least this exemplary case does show that there is justice for all,' remarked Daniel Talamoni, one of the four reporters who sued the World Cup winner.

'When the case began four years ago, everyone said it was impossible. They would sentence a man idolised in Argentina and forgive everything.'.

Arda Turan, with an unlicensed gun, in a Turkish hospital.

Sources indicate that keen fans of European football will not need to be reminded of who Arda Turan is. But they may be surprised to learn that the former Atletico Madrid and Barcelona star has had some serious trouble with the law.

Turan somehow avoided a jail sentence after discharging an unlicensed firearm in a hospital.

In 2018 while on loan from Barcelona in his home country of Turkey at Istanbul Basaksehir, Turan got into an altercation with Turkish singer Berkay Sahin, who ended in hospital with a broken nose.

Then Turan turned up at the hospital that was treating Sahin with an unlicensed firearm, and fired a shot into the floor.

He was eventually sentenced to two years and eight months behind bars for firing a gun to cause panic, illegal possession of weapons and intentional injury but the sentence was suspended for five years. Basaksehir also fined the midfielder £350,000 over the incident.

Nearly a decade after the incident, Turan now manages Ukrainian powerhouse Shakhtar Donetsk, joining the club in May of last year.

After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”.

“It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win swiftly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”.

At the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

Brighton knocked United out of the FA Cup in the third round, with Danny Welbeck scoring at Old Trafford, meaning the club played just 40 matches in 2025-26.

Carrick will want to make a better fist of the cup competitions, but he could really use a win of any kind after taking just four points from United’s first four league games of the fresh season.

Napoli vs Torino - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (673 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:19, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:21.
  • Separated by one place and one point, Napoli and Torino will return to Serie A duty on Saturday evening, when they meet at Stadio Maradona.
  • Both sides entered the international break on a grim run of form, sparking talk of another crisis for the hosts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:19, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:21.

Separated by one place and one point, Napoli and Torino will return to Serie A duty on Saturday evening, when they meet at Stadio Maradona.

Both sides entered the international break on a grim run of form, sparking talk of another crisis for the hosts.

After setting out with lofty ambitions, Napoli sit 10th in Serie A after 11 matchdays and have lost three of their first four Champions League fixtures.

Struggling both in Europe and Italy's top flight, the Partenopei have won just five times across all competitions since Massimiliano Allegri succeeded Antonio Conte.

That represents their lowest tally of wins at this stage of a campaign since 2003, when they drew 10 of their first 15 games down in Serie B.

Before international football intervened, Allegri's men did earn some credit by holding league leaders Lazio to a 1-1 home draw, having previously suffered damaging defeats to Juventus and Porto.

While they ended their visitors' streak of six consecutive wins - and spurned several second-half chances to seize victory - Napoli ultimately slipped further behind in the top four race.

As a result, the Campanian club cannot afford to drop many more points at the Maradona, where they beat Torino 2-1 in March - their 15th win from the last 22 league meetings.

Torino's only two triumphs during that period both came in Turin, so their last top-flight win in Naples dates all the way back to 2009.

Like their hosts, it has been a mixed start to the season under new management: Ignazio Abate's reign began slowly, but Toro then posted their best run of league wins for six years, before suddenly faltering again.

Having previously taken maximum points from three consecutive games, Toro lost to high-flyers Como and Frosinone, then went into the break with a disappointing home draw against Lecce.

Nonetheless, the Granata have claimed 14 points from their first 11 games for the fifth time in six years, leaving them just one behind Napoli in standings.

So, with a win this weekend, Abate can surpass his former Milan coach Allegri, as ambitious apprentice meets fading master.

Napoli form (all competitions):.

Napoli are still burdened by a significant absence list, but Allegri will have three players back at his disposal on Saturday: David Neres and Costantino Favasuli have recovered from muscular injuries, while Luca Marianucci has served his suspension.

Alisson Santos, Benoit Badiashile, Stanislav Lobotka, captain Giovanni Di Lorenzo and former Torino skipper Alessandro Buongiorno are still unavailable.

Having starred in Belgium's big UEFA Nations League victory over Italy, top scorer Kevin De Bruyne will aim to build on his six goal involvements for the Partenopei this season.

While speculation has been stirred up about De Bruyne's future, fan favourite Scott McTominay is set to stay put for now, and he has found the net three times in two games against Torino.

McTominay's international teammate Che Adams is Toro's leading Serie A scorer on four; the Scotland striker could partner Giovanni Simeone, who only scored six times in 83 league appearances for Napoli but has previously scored five goals against them.

Typically lining up just behind the front pair, Nikola Vlasic missed Sunday's clash between Croatia and the Czech Republic due to a minor thigh strain, but he is still expected to play this weekend.

However, Abate has fitness doubts regarding wing-backs Rafik Belghali, Ricardo Rodriguez and Niccolo Fortini.

Napoli possible starting lineup:.

Meret; Beukema, Rrahmani, Marin; Politano, Anguissa, De Bruyne, McTominay, Spinazzola; Vergara; Hojlund.

Torino possible starting lineup:.

Perri; Coco, Ismajli, Comuzzo; Belghali, Fitz-Jim, Mandragora, Cacciamani; Vlasic; Adams, Simeone.

After two defeats and one draw from their last three games, both teams will be desperate for a win.

While Napoli are hampered by injuries and appear disunited, Torino have been leaking too many goals, so more frustration could be on the cards.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Norwich City face off against Cardiff City off the back of a fantastic recent run of results, having won their last four games, scoring 15 goals in the process.

In a recent development, A revitalised NCFC will be looking to continue their march up the Championship table towards the play-off positions. The Canaries now sit 12th in the table with 21 points from 15 matches, three points off the top eight.

The visit of an inconsistent Cardiff City side presents a good opportunity to pick up three more points.

Brian Barry-Murphy‘s side head eastwards after two extraordinary home matches: a 3-3 draw against West Ham, where the Welsh outfit let slip a three-goal lead, before coming back from three goals down themselves to beat Burnley 5-4 last time out.

Norwich City have a number of longer term absentees.

In a recent development, ali Ahmed and Mohamed Toure remain injured. Having ruptured his ACL in pre-season, Ahmed will remain unavailable for the majority of the campaign and possibly longer, while Toure will return sooner and could be involved by the start of the Upcoming Year after his shoulder injury.

Having been out for about a month, Papa Amadou Diallo’s muscle injury will continue to keep him out of contention.

In a massive boost though, key midfielder Kenny McLean has used the international window to regain fitness and will now be at Clement’s disposal against Cardiff City.

Grimshaw; Stacey, Darling, McConville, Chrisene; Field, Wright; Brooks, Maghoma, Musaba; Kvistgaarden.

With no newly introduced injury concerns facing Clement’s side, the Norwich City team will likely remain unchanged after thrashing Bristol City in their last outing.

Dan Grimshaw keeps his place in goal with Vladan Kovacevic on the bench. The defence has been leaky at times this campaign, but after two clean sheets on the bounce, the NCFC boss will feel confident in maintaining the current backline.

It has been revealed that the central midfield two of Jacob Wright and Sam Field have started the last three games together, and the standard of their performances means they are set to get the nod ahead of Pelle Mattsson and returning captain McLean. Paris Maghoma will keep his spot in the advanced midfield position, having netted four goals in as many games.

Sources indicate that on the wings, Andre Brooks will play on the right having started every league game thus far. Anthony Musaba is set to hold down his place on the left after three consecutive starts, yielding two goals and an assist.

Mathias Kvistgaarden is the preferred starter over Makama, so expect the Dane to lead the line. Makama has two goals off the bench in his last two games, as well as earning his first England U21 cap during the international window, so he will be pushing for that starting place.

Norwich City vs Cardiff City kicks off at 12:30 on Saturday and will be broadcast live on Sky Sports+.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 18:47 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino enjoyed a stellar penultimate game in charge of the United States, thrashing Haiti 6-0.
  • The newly appointed Manchester United manager has just one game left before sinking his teeth into the job at Old Trafford.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:47 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 16 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino enjoyed a stellar penultimate game in charge of the United States, thrashing Haiti 6-0.

The newly appointed Manchester United manager has just one game left before sinking his teeth into the job at Old Trafford.

He will link up with United on Wednesday, but first must navigate the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final tie with Haiti on Tuesday.

Here, Pochettino cut a fairly reserved figure on the touchline as he was rewarded for trusting youth - and even saw his team score from a corner, something United don't do much of these days.

Without further ado, here are four things Manchester United fans learned from the win.

Mauricio Pochettino, dressed in a scarf, was fairly reserved as the United States beat Haiti 6-0.

According to recent reports, pochettino’s arrival spells good news for United’s proud tradition of promoting homegrown youth - it is glad tidings for the likes of Shea Lacey and Kobbie Mainoo. You wonder if, for a while, JJ Gabriel will look on forlornly from Real Madrid’s reserves.

The Argentinian handed out 13 debuts in the September-October international break, including to eight teenagers in one 4-1 victory over Peru.

It has been revealed that his strategy was no different here as he started 18-year-old Julian Hall up front and Diego Kochen, 20, in goal - both players he has given debuts to this year. He was rewarded, with Hall scoring his fourth goal in just five games for the United States, while Kochen kept a clean sheet.

Despite his affinity for the stars of tomorrow, he is a hard schoolmaster. In a column for The Athletic in 2022, he revealed that he sat a young Harry Kane down for a brutal meeting where he showed him stats and clips to justify why he wasn’t playing him more.

Pochettino had known Kane’s potential from their first training session but wanted the ‘tough conversation’ to get the best out of him. Kane went on to score 169 goals under him for Tottenham, and now he’s the best player in the world.

His trust in fresh faces could inject some much-needed enthusiasm around the club, strengthen the squad's connection with the fanbase, and increase the energy levels in one of the Premier League's oldest, most lethargic teams.

The likes of Shea Lacey will be delighted at how Pochettino puts trust in younger players.

Julian Hall, 18, struck his fourth goal in five games for the United States under Pochettino.

Pochettino has a history of getting the most out of attacking midfielders such as Dele Alli, Christian Eriksen, and Adam Lallana. You can add Cole Palmer to that list too, though he was primarily a right winger under him at Chelsea.

Manchester United desperately need him to get a tune out of Bruno Fernandes, who has cut a frustrated figure this season and whose creative efficiency has declined - though he still has nine goal involvements.

Industry observers note that if Christian Pulisic’s performance against Haiti is anything to go by, Fernandes will be happy. The attacking midfielder scored twice, playing a free role and being given penalty duty.

The 28-year-old was also asked to muck in defensively, and that’s something Fernandes is willing to do. Across the seasons, he has often covered more ground than any of his team-mates.

In a recent development, pochettino and Pulisic have seemingly had a distant relationship, despite the latter’s insistence to the contrary. The manager branded it ‘b*******’ when the AC Milan star opted out of the Gold Cup last year, and left him out of his selection a couple of months ago, bringing in 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan.

Asked about Pochettino's upcoming final game, Pulisic said at full-time: 'We're treating it like any other game.' No emotion on display.

Depending on how you interpret Fernandes - either a die-for-the-badge club servant or a primadonna - Pochettino could draw the best or worst out of the Portuguese.

Pochettino often gets the best out of attacking midfielders - will he work well with Bruno Fernandes?

He has had a distant relationship with Christian Pulisic, but the AC Milan star scored twice here.

Pochettino tends to push his defensive lines high up the pitch and his strategy with the United States has been no different.

They were almost caught out for trying to play the offside trap early on as a simple ball from midfield sent Danley Jean Jacques through one-on-one, forcing Kochen into a good save.

Meanwhile, full-backs Antonee Robinson and Alex Freeman were constantly pushing high and overlapping in his 4-2-3-1 system - although you’d obviously expect a strong level of intent when they’re favourites against Haiti.

Given his high-line tradition, Pochettino may well favour more mobile defenders such as Leny Yoro and Patrick Dorgu.

The battle for Harry Maguire will be to convince his fresh boss that his other qualities compensate for his lack of pace.

Pochettino takes inspiration from the frenetic football of Marcelo Bielsa, who managed him at Newell’s Old Boys in Argentina.

Recent findings suggest that but he'll have to balance his philosophy with the reality of United's woeful defensive record this campaign. Just the 15 goals conceded in the last five games...

Pochettino showed an eagerness to intervene early in the game - a possible boost after Michael Carrick suffered from slow starts.

Pochettino is typically seen as an animated character on the touchline, in contrast to Carrick's statesmanlike behaviour, but he spent lots of time in his seat here.

He has calmed down somewhat these days - though he did kick a crate of bottles in frustration at the World Cup - and didn’t even react much when his team scored.

In a recent development, A major criticism of Carrick is that he takes too long to change things in-game, often going late with substitutions. Pochettino has traditionally leaned that way, too, but he was eager to influence proceedings here.

Even three minutes in, at a break while Antonee Robinson was being treated, he called Pulisic over for what looked like an intense tactical chat.

According to recent reports, united have been plagued by slow starts this season, so it was encouraging to see Pochettino so alert and full of ideas early into the game. He could have coasted, really, but wanted to eke out every advantage.

Recent findings suggest that among the names linked have been Real Madrid’s Endrick, Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi and Sporting CP’s Goncalo Inacio. It’s one thing having the list of names, but it is another having the money and the possibility of doing a deal mid-season with the selling club.

During last night’s segment on Sky, Gianluca Di Marzio (via MilanNews) was asked whether Milan can realistically pursue names like Endrick and Tresoldi, who are likely to cost over €50m each.

“That they has the strength to do these kinds of deals, yes. They demonstrated it over the summer, so I don’t think there’s a financial issue,” he began.

“Whether they manage to sign one of the two… Endrick, as far as we know, José Mourinho hasn’t changed his mind and therefore doesn’t intend to part with him in January. But Endrick is a Cardinale obsession, just as he was a Roma obsession during the summer.

It has been revealed that “We’ll have to see if Mourinho changes his mind in the month and a half before the transfer window opens. He hasn’t changed his mind at the moment, so I see the situation as complicated at the moment.

“Just as it’s complicated for Brugge to sell Tresoldi. Brugge are a club that doesn’t need to sell and always sells at least one key player in the summer, precisely to try to get to the end of the season with its players.

Industry observers note that “Milan are looking for a striker, looking for a back-up for Ramos. The figures I’ve read, 60-70 million, are very, very high figures to try to convince Brugge to sell him. It’s a deal that – given the player’s objective value – I think is around 50 million. In my opinion.

Recent findings suggest that “But Brugge are unlikely to sell him in January. Above all, Milan is looking for a striker to be a back-up for Ramos; it’s not like Ramos and Tresoldi will play together. In the sense that Milan has always played with a centre-forward.

“Above all, they need to provide this center forward with plenty of playable balls rather than buy another. Because if Ramos doesn’t receive balls in the penalty area, he struggles to score, and Tresoldi struggles to score either.

“They need a striker to get Camarda playing. I think Camarda will go and play and therefore an investment will be needed in a player who can be a suitable deputy for Ramos.”.

Tech Report: Bayer Leverkusen vs SC Paderborn - prediction, team news, lineups
