💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Nolan | 19 Nov 2026 17:21, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:10.
  • Bayer Leverkusen will hope to keep pace with the Bundesliga's top four on Saturday, when they take on visitors SC Paderborn at BayArena.
  • The hosts come into the clash with 16 points after nine matchweeks and could end the weekend five points from the top four, whereas 13th-placed Paderborn have 10 points.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 19 Nov 2026 17:21, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:10.

Bayer Leverkusen will hope to keep pace with the Bundesliga's top four on Saturday, when they take on visitors SC Paderborn at BayArena.

The hosts come into the clash with 16 points after nine matchweeks and could end the weekend five points from the top four, whereas 13th-placed Paderborn have 10 points.

Leverkusen are two points from fourth-placed RB Leipzig and three points from third-placed Freiburg, but only four points separate them from 11th-placed Hamburger SV.

Manager Carles Martinez oversaw a 2-1 victory against FC Koln on November 8 prior to the international break, and that brought to an end a losing streak of two games.

The hosts have also lost two of their last three Bundesliga fixtures, conceding eight goals while scoring on four occasions.

Leverkusen's two most recent home clashes saw them lose 1-0 against Marseille in the Europa League on November 5 and 4-2 against Stuttgart in the German top flight on October 31.

However, it should be noted that they triumphed in each of their first five clashes at BayArena this season, netting at least two goals in each contest.

Paderborn were held to a 2-2 stalemate by Eintracht Frankfurt on November 7 before the international break, and that extended their undefeated streak in the league to four outings.

The club only won once in that time, while they managed to score five goals and keep two clean sheets, with all four of the goals they conceded coming in two separate 2-2 draws.

Head coach Ralf Kettemann will hope to earn a first away victory in five matches, though a draw would be the club's fourth in that period.

The visitors have failed to find the back of the net in three of their four Bundesliga matches on the road this campaign, though they also prevented opponents from scoring twice.

A win for Paderborn would be their first ever success against Leverkusen, with the hosts having beaten the visitors in six of their seven meetings.

Bayer Leverkusen Bundesliga form:.

Bayer Leverkusen form (all competitions):.

SC Paderborn form (all competitions):.

Leverkusen do not have to deal with any major absences, though attackers Nathan Tella, Martin Terrier and Christian Kofane are set to miss out.

There is no reason to doubt the inclusion of Patrik Schick as the hosts' striker, while a supporting cast of Moussa Diaby, Ibrahim Maza and Afonso Moreira could complete an exciting frontline.

Midfielders Aleix Garcia and Ezequiel Fernandez are likely candidates for the team's double pivot, and they may play ahead of centre-backs Edmond Tapsoba and Facundo Medina.

Paderborn's only confirmed absentee is attacker Timur Gayret, who is not scheduled to return until January due to a knee injury.

It would not be surprising to see the visitors field a front two of Marvin Pieringer and Stefano Marino ahead of midfielders Tom Baack, Santiago Castaneda and Gabriel Vidovic.

Bayer Leverkusen possible starting lineup:.

Flekken; Quansah, Tapsoba, Medina, Gutierrez; Garcia, Fernandez; Diaby, Maza, Moreira; Schick.

SC Paderborn possible starting lineup:.

Noll; Ter Horst, Scheller, Hansen; Curda, Baack, Castaneda, Vidovic, Obermair; Pieringer, Marino.

Leverkusen's recent form at home is concerning, though they have proven in the past that they are capable of regularly finding the back of the net at BayArena.

Paderborn have been stubborn at times, though they have struggled for results on the road, so perhaps they will fail to take any points on the weekend.

Stoke City vs Birmingham City - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (634 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 17:22.
  • After both swapping their typical midtable mediocrity for an exciting promotion race, Stoke City and Birmingham City clash at the bet365 Stadium for a Championship match on Saturday afternoon.
  • The Potters enjoyed a dramatic success at Portsmouth prior to the November international break, whilst Blues picked up a last-minute victory over Swansea City in the Second City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 17:22.

After both swapping their typical midtable mediocrity for an exciting promotion race, Stoke City and Birmingham City clash at the bet365 Stadium for a Championship match on Saturday afternoon.

The Potters enjoyed a dramatic success at Portsmouth prior to the November international break, whilst Blues picked up a last-minute victory over Swansea City in the Second City.

In the build-up to this weekend, Stoke head coach Mark Robins has revealed that a top-eight finish was the target set in August, however, it appears that his Staffordshire outfit could be capable of much more.

After losing their first three matches, the Potters have been defeated in just one of their past 12 second-tier contests - a run which includes four wins and a single draw in their past five clashes.

Before the final international break of the calendar year, Stoke made it three straight victories with a 2-1 triumph at Fratton Park, where second-half goals from Jack McGlynn and Ben Wilmot secured maximum points.

With their sole defeat since August coming against promotion favourites Middlesbrough, Robins's men have flown up to third position in the Championship table, level on points with leaders Birmingham.

For all of the positivity around the Potters, they have not been untouchable at the bet365 Stadium in recent times, managing just a single win over bottom side Preston North End across their past three home contests.

After a humiliating 6-1 defeat by Brentford in the EFL Cup on August 25, many Birmingham City supporters were calling for the head of manager Chris Davies, who has since masterminded a remarkable turnaround in the Second City.

Between the past two international breaks, Blues have established themselves as the team to beat in the Championship, winning six of their past seven league fixtures, including four straight home successes.

Following comfortable St Andrew's @ Knighthead Park wins over Preston (4-0), Queens Park Rangers (3-0) and Millwall (3-0), Birmingham needed a last-gasp Jay Stansfield goal to conquer Swansea on November 7.

Scoring on three occasions in the past two matches, £20m man Stansfield stepped up to the goalscoring plate in the absence of August Priske, with Max Bird entering the starting XI and also performing excellently.

Rather remarkably, Blues are sitting on the summit of the Championship table for the first time since the 2008-09 season - the campaign in which they last secured promotion to the Premier League under Alex McLeish.

Birmingham City Championship form:.

Stoke have a number of injury doubts ahead of this weekend's top-of-the-table clash, including youngster Lamine Cisse and defender Eric Bocat.

Providing plenty of experience to the Potters ranks, Aaron Cresswell has not featured since May in a competitive game due to a knee problem.

Scoring for Slovakia in the Nations League on Monday, striker Robert Bozenik arrives back in Staffordshire full of confidence.

Birmingham boast international stars of their own, with Colombia's Jhon Solis and Canada's Liam Millar returning from duty unscathed.

Sitting out of selection for their nations over the past fortnight, goalkeeper James Beadle and Priske are both available for this weekend.

As a result, second-choice stopper Ryan Allsop will likely return to the bench and Bird could drop out of the XI despite impressive displays recently.

Stoke City possible starting lineup:.

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Tchamadeu, Soumare, Galbraith, Johnson; McGlynn, Manhoef, Bozenik.

Birmingham City possible starting lineup:.

Beadle; Laird, Neumann, Klarer, Cochrane; Iwata, Solis; Roberts, Stansfield, Millar; Priske.

Both camps will realise the significance of Saturday's match as two of the Championship's unexpected title challengers lock horns.

Consequently, it could be a cagey affair between the pair, who would be content with a share of the spoils.

#26808. Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

📅 17 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 20m • 📚 Deep Dive (4071 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

📅 17 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4071 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.
  • This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.
  • But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

It has been revealed that so to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

Industry observers note that “I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a substantial career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”.

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

According to recent reports, what a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy.

Recent findings suggest that “It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca stated. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”.

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

According to recent reports, allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL.

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has mentioned supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was vital for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca noted.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

Recent findings suggest that FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

According to recent reports, all told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

In a recent development, with the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:.

Possession: Man City 66% vs 34% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 30 vs 4.

Industry observers note that erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Industry observers note that mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Another round of changes for both sides.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Recent findings suggest that lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Sources indicate that significant cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

It has been revealed that well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

Sources indicate that what a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

In a recent development, norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

It has been revealed that maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

Norwich take off Diallo for Maghoma.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:.

Possession: Man City 72% vs 28% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 15 vs 1.

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

It has been revealed that samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

According to recent reports, A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

Recent findings suggest that and the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

In a recent development, norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Sources indicate that another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Recent findings suggest that spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

Industry observers note that it’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

We have kicked off in Manchester!

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:.

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba.

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo.

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden.

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré.

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU.

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX.

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a newly introduced five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF.

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here.

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

It has been revealed that his older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

In a recent development, city fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Checking in 🚌🚶‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/xWYGyaH7TY.

Manchester City or Norwich vs Brighton.

Ⓒ Darling with the armband🧤 Grimshaw in goal⚡️ Ante on the rightYour Yellows for this evening ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/znOGtvyJyk.

Your City side to take on Norwich 👊XI | Rulli, Lewis, Khusanov, Reis, O'Reilly, Bouaddi, Kovačić (C), Samba, Allan, Aït-Nouri, CherkiSUBS | Donnarumma, Anderson, Guéhi, Ndiaye, Fernández, Nunes, Semenyo, McAidoo, Braithwaite🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/LCA4WfACBf.

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

Recent findings suggest that these two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blackburn Rovers face rivals Burnley on Sunday, and the substantial story leading up to the game has been Tony Mowbray’s withdrawal from head coach duties due to health issues.
  • As relayed by local reporter Elliott Jackson, Johnson revealed that star striker Andri Gudjohnsen and midfield mainstay Sam Morsy are alongside Scott Wharton in requiring assessment before the game.
  • One man whose fate has already been confirmed is Balazs Toth, after the goalkeeper broke a finger while away with Hungary.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blackburn Rovers face rivals Burnley on Sunday, and the substantial story leading up to the game has been Tony Mowbray’s withdrawal from head coach duties due to health issues. Damien Johnson is stepping into the role in the interim, and he and the first-team staff have a handful of injuries to deal with.

As relayed by local reporter Elliott Jackson, Johnson revealed that star striker Andri Gudjohnsen and midfield mainstay Sam Morsy are alongside Scott Wharton in requiring assessment before the game. All other players returning from international duty – Tom Atcheson, Augustus Kargbo and Kristi Montgomery – will be tested as well, Johnson has stated.

One man whose fate has already been confirmed is Balazs Toth, after the goalkeeper broke a finger while away with Hungary. In better news though, Japanese playmaker Ryoya Morishita has trained over the break and is expected to be available.

Among those requiring assessment, there are some crucial Blackburn Rovers players.

Industry observers note that striker Gudjohnsen is perhaps the most crucial player in blue and white halves at the moment. The Icelandic talisman is in unassailable form, with 11 goals in 15 club games alongside four in two while away with his national side over the latest international break.

Morsy has become an influential player since his summer arrival. It perhaps wasn’t expected that he would become such a key starter, but his partnership in midfield with Montgomery has given this Rovers side some experience and bite. Ahead of a high-stakes game with aggression and tough tackles expected, having the Egyptian in the middle of the park will be key.

Toth is a major loss though, so it will be down to Aynsley Pears to step in. Sunday would have been a fitting game for Blackburn-born favourite Wharton to return, but there is understandable patience over his comeback.

In a recent development, morishita’s return is a big boost, however. The 29-year-old is a key creative source, and even if he can only play from the bench, he can still make a telling impact.

Now, there’s no reason to doubt Johnson’s update, but sections of the Blackburn Rovers support will be hoping that there isn’t as much doubt surrounding the likes of Gudjohnsen and Morsy as has been let on.

Indecisive answers on their availability keep Burnley guessing. The rigorous preparation clubs go through before games nowadays means the Clarets will be prepared for all outcomes, but the uncertainty means they have to stay on their toes and plan carefully for all potential lineups.

Sources indicate that one thing for sure is that all of Rovers’ doubts will be doing whatever they can to be fit for the fixture. Not only is this a great chance to end a 16-year wait for an East Lancashire derby win, but the players and staff will be determined to deliver a result for Mowbray after he stepped back earlier this week.

Tech Report: 'Am I supposed to answer that?': Erling Haaland breaks silence and distances himself from Man City cheating verdict as star striker insists 'I don't really know much... I was playing for Bryne Under 9s'

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 09:50 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Erling Haaland delivered a monologue of over two minutes detailing the teams he represented in the years covered by the Premier League's investigation into Man City, as the star questioned how he was meant to respond to the club's guilty verdict.
  • Sources indicate that man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 09:50 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 16 November 2026.

Erling Haaland delivered a monologue of over two minutes detailing the teams he represented in the years covered by the Premier League's investigation into Man City, as the star questioned how he was meant to respond to the club's guilty verdict.

Sources indicate that man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September. The club have since appealed.

An independent commission ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period with ‘sham’ deals.

Man City were found to have artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

Haaland was quizzed about the club's situation by Norwegian broadcaster TV2, after scoring in the national team's 3-1 victory over Wales on Saturday.

The Man City star's initial answer lasted for two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges.

Erling Haaland insisted it was difficult for him to answer a question about Man City's guilty verdict, with the club appealing against the decision of an independent commission. Source: TV2Sport.

Haaland stressed he remains happy at the club after being asked about his future given the potential ramificiations if Man City fail with their appeal to overturn the verdict.

'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland began.

'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle….

Sources indicate that 'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'.

Haaland continued by listing fellow Norwegians who had been at Man City at the time, joking that they may be in a better place to offer insight.

'There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think,' Haaland remarked.

'Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can't remember.

Recent findings suggest that the forward distanced himself from the case as he listed team he played from 2009-18, the time covered by the charges. Pictured: Haaland in action for Molde in 2018.

'But it's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

Sources indicate that 'A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a newly introduced nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that states everything about the matter. I'm a City player, and I'm incredibly happy there.'.

Man City have continued to insist they had 'irrefutable evidence' proving their innocence, but if the club loses its appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

Haaland, who has won eight major honours at the club including the Treble in 2023, was asked about whether the case has affected his thoughts on his Man City future.

'I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,' Haaland responded.

'I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that. I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.

'I'm standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we're top of our group in Europe.

'Things aren't going so well for City in the league, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can't focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.'.

Man City have won twice and lost three times in the Premier League since the independent commission verdict was announced in September.

Enzo Maresca's side have slipped to six points behind reigning champions Arsenal following their drop off in form.

Como vs Cagliari - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:24, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:27.
  • Having left for the international break on a rare low, Como will aim to resume their stellar start to the season when Cagliari visit Stadio Sinigaglia on Saturday.
  • Not only are the Lariani making a big impact in Europe, they have been breaking latest ground in Serie A - but defeat to the champions recently slowed their charge towards the top four.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:24, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:27.

Having left for the international break on a rare low, Como will aim to resume their stellar start to the season when Cagliari visit Stadio Sinigaglia on Saturday.

Not only are the Lariani making a big impact in Europe, they have been breaking latest ground in Serie A - but defeat to the champions recently slowed their charge towards the top four.

Como have caught the eye in this season's Champions League - notably following their famous 4-1 defeat of Manchester United with a ruthless 9-1 destruction of Lens - and they also have massive ambitions in Serie A.

Remarkably, the European rookies sit above Barcelona and Bayern Munich in UEFA's top competition, and they had posted six straight wins across all competitions before facing Inter Milan last time out.

Overseen by one of football's most-wanted coaches, the Lariani scored 22 goals and conceded just four during that hot streak, but it came to an abrupt end at San Siro.

Como's 12th consecutive league defeat to Inter left Cesc Fabregas and co five points behind the Scudetto holders, while costing them their place in the top four.

As a manager, Fabregas has yet to conquer Inter in either Serie A or the Coppa Italia, but his team tend to take care of business against Italy's lesser lights.

Now heading back to base, Como have kept clean sheets in their last three league matches at the Sinigaglia, where they have never lost a top-flight clash against Cagliari.

Beaten 2-1 when the pair most recently met, Cagliari's last Serie A win over Como dates back to March 1982 - albeit both clubs have spent plenty of time outside the top tier.

This term, the Sardinian side will head to Lombardy full of confidence, as they sit just inside the top half following a largely positive start to the current campaign.

Hurtling out of the blocks, Fabio Pisacane's men claimed four victories from their opening five fixtures - only losing to Inter - before slipping back into the pack with a less successful run.

Yet, when facing down Frosinone after suffering four consecutive defeats, Cagliari came out on top: Michel Adopo's goal gave them a 1-0 win over the newly promoted high-flyers.

All told, a haul of 16 points from their first 11 matches represents the Rossoblu's best top-flight start since 2019, and Pisacane has been handed much of the credit.

Continuing an injury-hit start to his Como career, Moise Kean has suffered a setback in his recovery from a tibia problem and could be sidelined for several more weeks.

Wide men Jayden Addai and Jesus Rodriguez are also unavailable, but Fabregas hopes to have Assane Diao and Trevoh Chalobah back in the squad.

The hosts' star man, Nico Paz helped Argentina beat Costa Rica 7-0 earlier this week, scoring his first international brace.

Sources indicate that the 22-year-old has already posted 14 goal involvements for Como this season, attracting interest from Europe's top clubs. Curiously, though, just two of his last 11 Serie A strikes have come on home soil.

While Paz should link up with Greece striker Tasos Douvikas in the final third, Cagliari's front line may be led by Paul Mendy and Daniel Maldini - the latter of whom has found the net five times this term.

Although Pisacane can recall Adam Obert after the left-back served a suspension against Frosinone, several men are still missing through injury.

Alieu Fadera and Mattia Felici have been ruled out, while M'Bala Nzola (flexor), Harry Winks (back) and Yerry Mina (thigh) are all struggling to return in time.

Butez; Couto, Kempf, Ramon, Valle; Perrone, Milla; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas.

Cagliari possible starting lineup:.

Caprile; Ze Pedro, Kofler, Rodriguez, Obert; Adopo, Romano, Deiola; Fazzini, Maldini; Mendy.

Free-flowing Como can score from all quarters, while Cagliari must head to the mainland on a run of three away defeats, in which they shipped 10 goals.

So, the hosts will resume winning ways after their setback in Milan, keeping them on the tails of Italy's top three.

Burnley team news and predicted XI to face Blackburn Rovers as key player returns for derby day

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fabio Celestini has inherited a sinking ship with the monumental task of keeping Burnley afloat, with the international break arriving at the perfect time to put a temporary halt to their struggle.
  • The Clarets’ 5-4 capitulation at Cardiff City, where they were leading 4-1 by the 62nd minute, was a brutal reminder of where they find themselves.
  • Sources indicate that as it stands, Burnley sit 22nd in the Championship table with just one win in 15 games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fabio Celestini has inherited a sinking ship with the monumental task of keeping Burnley afloat, with the international break arriving at the perfect time to put a temporary halt to their struggle.

The Clarets’ 5-4 capitulation at Cardiff City, where they were leading 4-1 by the 62nd minute, was a brutal reminder of where they find themselves. Celestini’s squad are devoid of confidence and leaking goals at will.

Sources indicate that as it stands, Burnley sit 22nd in the Championship table with just one win in 15 games. They are already five points from safety and lurking in the bottom three alongside Derby County and Preston North End.

Blackburn Rovers meanwhile will feel they can finally end their 16-year wait for a victory over their arch rivals, buoyed by a 2-1 victory over promotion-chasing West Ham last time out.

Anel Ahmedhodzic could return to the fold having missed the trip to Cardiff City due to illness, but Conor Roberts will be absent after a red card in South Wales and will serve the first match of his three-game suspension.

According to recent reports, injuries have been an unfortunate feature of Dastan Satpayev’s time at Turf Moor since arriving on loan from Chelsea and he remains out with a recurring hamstring glitch. Tunisian international Hannibal Mejbri will be absent with the same injury.

Sources indicate that the defeat at Lincoln City brought an end to Nicky Hayen’s time in charge, and it also brought Amando Broja’s season to a temporary standstill with a groin injury. Fellow frontman Ashley Barnes remains out, but is nearing a return after featuring for the U21s side.

Jacob Bruun Larsen is out due to a stress fracture and Jordan Beyer remains a long-term absentee and is yet to make a competitive appearance since December 2023 due to a serious knee injury. Among those also unavailable are Ben Amos, Mike Tresor, Shurandy Sambo and Michael Obafemi.

In better news, Bashir Humphreys has been back in training and is on the brink of a return. The Blackburn Rovers clash may come too soon, but he could return next week.

Coudert; Walker, Ahmedhodzic, Ekdal, Pires; Cullen, Hatate; Ramazani, Edwards, Banel; Vardy.

Due to injuries, Celestini’s side pretty much picks for itself. However, there could be one key change in midfield.

Gregoire Coudert has only kept two clean sheets this term, but will line up between the sticks.

Gregoire Coudert’s Burnley stats.

The full-back flanks will be occupied by Kyle Walker on the right and Lucas Pires on the left, while the returning Ahmedhodzic could partner Hjalmar Ekdal at centre-back in place of Igor Julio.

Josh Laurent and Reo Hatate have been the midfield pivot for the last two outings, but after three appearances off the bench, club captain and star player Josh Cullen could return to the starting lineup for the first time since his ACL injury in December 2025.

Marcus Edwards plays in attacking midfield, and with two goals in three games under Celestini, the right-wing position will likely fall to the in-form Largie Ramazani. Jayden Banel plays off the left.

The centre-forward spot is the one position which is up for grabs, with Andreas Hountondji beginning to show signs of promise. However, the experience of Jamie Vardy could prove crucial in a game of this significance.

Burnley vs Blackburn Rovers kicks off at 12:00 on Sunday, and will be broadcast live on Sky Sports Football and ITV.

Crystal Palace injury news: Thomas Frank update on Ismaila Sarr, Takehiro Tomiyasu before Coventry clash

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (488 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 18:35, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 18:36.
  • Thomas Frank has provided his first injury enhancement as Crystal Palace manager ahead of Saturday’s Premier League clash with Coventry City at the CBS Arena.
  • Nine months after his sacking by Tottenham Hotspur, Frank was appointed the upcoming Eagles boss on Monday, just five days after Pierre Sage was relieved of his duties.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 18:35, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 18:36.

Thomas Frank has provided his first injury enhancement as Crystal Palace manager ahead of Saturday’s Premier League clash with Coventry City at the CBS Arena.

Nine months after his sacking by Tottenham Hotspur, Frank was appointed the upcoming Eagles boss on Monday, just five days after Pierre Sage was relieved of his duties.

The Dane has taken over a Palace side that sits rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of their opening 10 top-flight fixtures, including a 3-1 home defeat to Liverpool before the international break.

Defender Takehiro Tomiyasu has been sidelined for the last nine matches in all competitions with a calf injury, while last season’s top scorer Ismaila Sarr has been limited to only 15 minutes of Premier League action this term due to an ongoing groin problem.

Speaking at a press conference on Thursday afternoon, Frank confirmed that both players will not be ready to return for the trip to Coventry.

According to recent reports, "I can say that Tomiyasu will be back training next week," Frank told reporters. "On Sarr, it'll be touch and go when he can start training. It's a groin injury so you need to be careful.

"You need to be aware with those injuries about how much you push. That could take a little longer time. You need to make sure that you don't take two steps forward, to then take two steps back.

Recent findings suggest that "This could take a little longer. He'll not necessarily be on the pitch next week.".

Chadi Riad (knee) remains a long-term injury absentee for Palace, while there was no mention of Jorgen Strand Larsen at Frank’s press conference, but the striker has been spotted in training this week after withdrawing from the Norway squad with an ankle matter.

Meanwhile, striker Jean-Philippe Mateta will serve the second of a three-match suspension this weekend following his red card against Tottenham at the end of last month.

Palace are hoping for an immediate manager bounce under Frank following a disappointing run of four straight defeats in the Premier League.

The Eagles won their first four visits to the CBS Arena between 2005 and 2008, but are winless in their last four across all tournaments between 2009 and their most recent trip in 2012 (D2 L2).

Discussing the challenge of facing Coventry in his first game as Palace boss, Frank noted: "I know it'll be difficult.

In a recent development, "But I also trust the boys, I know we'll perform on Saturday. We just need a little margin to go in our favour.".

Victory for Palace could see them climb off the foot of the table and out of the relegation zone up to as high as 16th place – above Coventry currently in 17th – if other results go their way this weekend.

Starting with Mike Maignan, both he and the French medical staff have reassured Milan regarding the physical issue that forced the goalkeeper to be substituted at half-time during Sunday’s match between Les Bleus and Turkey.

The Rossoneri captain took a knock to the hip area and felt some discomfort in his right adductor. No medical examinations were conducted while he was away, but they have been scheduled for early this afternoon.

In a recent development, maignan has put the club at ease, stating that he is not in any pain. Yesterday evening, he posted a photo of himself preparing to make a save, perhaps a way of saying he is ready. However, Lorenzo Torriani is on stand-by if needed.

Meanwhile, yesterday afternoon, Fikayo Tomori and Ruben Loftus-Cheek underwent examinations to assess their recovery from their respective muscle injuries. The tests took place in London, where both players spent the week off granted by the coaching staff.

The news is encouraging, and the recovery process is progressing well: the injury to the defender’s medial flexor in his right thigh is healing, and he will begin gradual work on the pitch over the coming days.

Industry observers note that whether he will be available against Frosinone or for the Europa League match against Olympiakos remains to be seen. The injury sustained against Bologna in late October is nearly behind him, but no unnecessary risks will be taken.

#26779. Tech Report: 'Managers now are b****y boring!': NEIL WARNOCK on the lack of characters in football, his friendship with Pep Guardiola, why he is open to managing again post-Christmas - and how he almost became a chiropodist!

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1427 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: 'Managers now are b****y boring!': NEIL WARNOCK on the lack of characters in football, his friendship with Pep Guardiola, why he is open to managing again post-Christmas - and how he almost became a chiropodist!

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1427 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 19:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Spending time in the company of Neil Warnock is always an education, be it witnessing one of his legendary foul-mouthed touchline rants or perched at one of his stage shows at grand venues like London Palladium.
  • On this occasion, Daily Mail Sport is perched in an east London bar watching on as one of English football's national treasures is posing for some modelling.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 19:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 16 November 2026.

Spending time in the company of Neil Warnock is always an education, be it witnessing one of his legendary foul-mouthed touchline rants or perched at one of his stage shows at grand venues like London Palladium.

On this occasion, Daily Mail Sport is perched in an east London bar watching on as one of English football's national treasures is posing for some modelling. Yes, you read that right, Mr Warnock is here to launch his own pair of socks with a tipple of Famous Grouse whisky in hand.

The complements on Warnock's 77-year-old feet are soon over, though, and we can get on to talking about a life in football that started six decades ago as a winger for Chesterfield and has traversed 10 clubs as a player, 17 as a manager and more than 2,000 games in the dugout.

So where to start? Maybe his reflections on nearly five decades in management – and how the whole conversation about feet is not too out of place….

'You don't realise how long it has been really, I started off just a team of ragamuffins as I call them,' he says in his iconic Yorkshire accent. 'They used to train on the green where I had digs in Hartlepool and asked me to coach them.

Sources indicate that 'I remember we scored from a set-piece we worked on, I was running up and down the touchline high-fiving everyone. I got the bug. I knew I could never get to the top as a player, I was quick but I was brainless.

Daily Mail Sport caught up with Neil Warnock to discuss his six decades in football.

After representing 10 different clubs as a player, Warnock became one of the most compelling managers in the game.

Industry observers note that 'I could've been a chiropodist if not in football. That could be on a quiz, couldn't it? I had bad feet at Scunthorpe, I used to get massive blisters so the physio there started getting me to do some of the players' feet.

Sources indicate that 'I enjoyed doing ingrown toenails and things like that! So I thought why not? Then I had a practice in Sheffield. I had to make a decision when we won the league at Scarborough whether to go full-time or pack it in. I thought, "Oh, go on then, let's give it a little go".

'It's not worked out badly, really, has it?

'People come up to me every day and say, "You're a legend, you". And I say, "Oh, thank you very much". Then they tell me what club they support, I have had so many haven't I? Last week I went out for a minute and had four selfies. They all appreciate what I did for their club.

'There aren't as many characters in the game now, you wouldn't get upset with managers now like in my day because now they are that b****y boring! Some of them barely speak.

According to recent reports, 'They won't get the rapport we had. I managed at a good time. The way I managed, I needed that humour. I needed the lads to enjoy it. I signed a lot of players that many managers wouldn't touch with a barge pole, are you with me? They ended up getting me promotions.'.

The aforementioned humour brings us on to a private conversation he had with the great Pep Guardiola, one of the millions of anecdotes up Warnock's sleeve but one that he has not told until now.

In a recent development, 'I went to a training session and he asked me to say a few words,' explains Warnock. 'I said, "Well lads I bet you're glad I'm not your manager because we'd be kicking balls from there to there, chasing it, heading it, practicing our tackles"... everyone laughed.

Warnock views Pep Guardiola as the best manager of his lifetime, while the Spaniard praised the veteran's humour after once addressing his Man City squad at a training session.

Warnock has led teams to promotions on eight occasions over the course of his career.

In a recent development, 'After the session we had a coffee and Pep noted to me, "Neil, that was amazing, you know when you talked to the players? I understood why you had so many promotions".

In a recent development, 'He started counting and said, "What we have is all these staff… computers, details, nutritionist, all these staff, but you know what we don't have? Humour". He noticed why my lads had done well in my teams, just in that meeting. It was good, that. He is amazing.

Industry observers note that 'Pep is the best manager of my lifetime. They say he had all the best players but it is not easy managing them. Pep did things with players and now there are non-league teams trying to play like Manchester City!'.

Warnock is now doing stage tours - Guardiola attended one last season - and had a tear in his eye when he stepped out at London Palladium given he used to watch shows there with his mother, who was in a wheelchair, on the TV as a child.

According to recent reports, so what is Warnock up to these days? His current role is advisor at Torquay United but last management job was at Aberdeen two years ago… so is he out of the rat race for good this time?

Industry observers note that 'No, not really, no,' he says. 'I only work from February to April! So the phone will be on after Christmas. You never know, do ya? There will be someone thinking "why don't we get that Warnock in?".

According to recent reports, 'I've retired 40 times! Every time I have stated it, I have meant it. But it's that dressing room camaraderie. There's something about football, when I look at some of the managers now… they just don't excite me.

Sources indicate that 'I remember Ruben Amorim (breaks down laughing). He's got his computer out on the bench! I remember watching and thinking, "I'm sorry, son, you need more than a computer to help you tonight!".

Warnock is currently doing stage tours, with Guardiola among the attendees last season.

Warnock's current role is advisor at Torquay United and briefly served as interim manager last season, with the 77-year-old admitting he had not completely ruled out a return to the dugout.

'And likewise, I see them making notes on the bench, oh my god. I think "what are you doing, your shopping list for Tescos?".

In a recent development, 'I do enjoy walking and I enjoy photography, believe it or not. I go up the river with my phone, there's so many lovely things to see.

It has been revealed that 'I've got an electric bike and I sometimes do about 25 miles. I was thinking of doing a cycle of all my clubs but that would take me five years! They go at about 30mph down the hills, you've got to be careful, you wouldn't want to come off them.'.

He is also enjoying fishing, being with the family and playing golf with his son, a PGA rising star William - though Warnock Sr insists he often embarrasses himself playing off 'the ladies' tee'.

The thing that makes Warnock most proud is the four promotions at Wembley but also the togetherness he fostered in his many teams.

It has been revealed that he tells us: 'What I like about the teams I had, they all have reunions. You look at the tele now, someone will score a goal and kiss the badge… they won't have a reunion.

'When I go to these reunions, I see all my lads and how I blended that dressing room together and I look at the comradeship they still have now, they are the same as they were just a lot older.

'This year, my Scarborough team are having a 40-year celebration and the lads have invited me. I said there's no way I'm going out with that lot after the do because they can drink, let me tell you!'.

* The Famous Grouse has teamed up with Happy Socks to launch an exclusive limited-edition collection, available at Tesco stores across the UK. Shoppers can pick up a free pair of colourful, collectable socks with selected 70cl bottles of The Famous Grouse whisky, priced from £18.50. Available in-store only, while stocks last.

Thomas Frank makes exciting Crystal Palace promise after trading Australia break for Premier League return

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (734 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 18:49.
  • New Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank has vowed to give his “very best” to ensure that the Eagles will avoid relegation from the Premier League this season.
  • The 53-year-old was officially unveiled as Palace’s upcoming boss on Monday, just five days after the sacking of his predecessor Pierre Sage who lasted less than five months at Selhurst Park.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 18:49.

New Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank has vowed to give his “very best” to ensure that the Eagles will avoid relegation from the Premier League this season.

The 53-year-old was officially unveiled as Palace’s upcoming boss on Monday, just five days after the sacking of his predecessor Pierre Sage who lasted less than five months at Selhurst Park.

Frank has taken over an Eagles outfit that is sitting rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of their opening 10 games and conceding a division-high 24 goals.

The Dane was believed to be on Palace’s radar in the summer, but he made it clear that he wanted an extended break away from management before assessing his options.

Frank now feels that the time is right to return to the Premier League “circus” for the first time since he was sacked by Tottenham Hotspur in February after a underwhelming eight-month spell in charge, winning just 34.2% of his 38 games in North London.

Remembered fondly for his successful seven-year tenure as Brentford boss, Frank is excited to take the reins at an “iconic” club in the form of Crystal Palace and is confident that he can steer them away from trouble.

It has been revealed that speaking at his first press conference on Thursday afternoon ahead of Saturday’s Premier League clash at Coventry City, Frank told reporters: "It's good to be back! It's a little bit of surprise, the feeling I have in the body; how good it feels.

"Of course I stated yes for a reason, to join Palace and go back into the circus and into the Premier League.

"It's just so good to be back and I'm in no doubt there won't be times where it won't feel like that, but I'm happy to be here.".

"For me Palace is an iconic club in England and it's also shown that, in many years in the Premier League, doing fantastic things,” Frank added.

"Selhurst Park is a fantastic place to go, to watch football, to feel the atmosphere, to feel a proper game.

Sources indicate that "I think Palace, when I've faced them over the years have always been a tough team to play. It's always been difficult.".

Frank was enjoying a break away from football in Australia with his family, but he was persuaded by Crystal Palace to return to the Premier League in the middle of a season.

Sources indicate that "It's been of course extremely busy. In every aspect, of course, to join a pre-season is a privilege and I've had the privilege to do that in the other clubs I've been in,” mentioned the Dane.

"The good thing is that you want to implement all your ideas, and that will take some time to hit the ground running, but I know what I want and the direction we should go in.

"Timing - in life and football - is everything. I was enjoying my life in Australia. It's pretty nice down there. Nice weather together with the family. And I'm a person that really enjoys football, it is my life. It's scary to feel how I feel, how it feels to be back.

In a recent development, "I'll speak to my good friend Roy [Hodgson] of course and speak to him - I don't want to go as long as he did - but it's good, that feeling. Good to be back.".

Commenting on improving results at Selhurst Park and moving away from the relegation zone, Frank added: "I'm looking forward to come in to do everything I can to help the team, the club.

"I think it's a very talented squad. I think it's got good potential in every aspect.

"Of course we are in a position where we don't want to be, and I'll do my very best together with the staff and players to make sure we're in a much better position when the season is done.".

Crystal Palace, who have spent the last 14 years in the top flight, could climb out of the relegation zone if they end their four-match losing streak with a victory at Coventry this weekend and other results go their way.

Meanwhile, Frank has also provided a fresh injury enhancement on attacker Ismaila Sarr and defender Takehiro Tomiyasu ahead of their trip to the CBS Arena.

Wolves host Charlton Athletic this weekend as they look to go top of the Championship table with a win. Cesar Peixoto’s side are currently 4th in the table but are just one point behind Birmingham City, Middlesbrough and Stoke City ahead of them.

Ahead of the Charlton clash, Peixoto has been speaking to The Express and Star providing a full enhancement on his squad. The Wolves boss had plenty of positive news, including that Fer Lopez is closing in on a return to full fitness.

Recent findings suggest that “Fer did not train in the first week (of the international break) because he was recovering from injury.” stated Peixoto. “Fer had a good week of training. We had to manage him on Thursday, but he trained well and needed this kind of training with the team.

It has been revealed that “Fer is not 100 per cent. He has a little pain, but nothing important at this stage. But we are going to see a better Fer, because when he came back from the previous international break he was injured and played with pain.

According to recent reports, “We have to manage the minutes with him. He is an important player for us. But I think he will be better than before.”.

Peixoto also mentioned that Jean-Ricner Bellegarde and Jordan James have trained on Thursday and Friday but are not 100%. On another positive note, Bertrand Traore and Boubacar Traore have returned to full training.

Lopez has emerged as one of Wolves’ most influential players this season, with the 22-year-old making an impressive impact following his return from a loan spell at Celta Vigo.

In a recent development, the Spanish attacking midfielder has scored six goals and provided three assists in 14 Championship appearances, accumulating 1,097 minutes and an average rating of 7.58, according to FotMob. He has also contributed a goal in the Carabao Cup, taking his overall return to seven goals and three assists in 16 appearances.

In a recent development, the summer 2025 signing has become a key figure under Peixoto, helping Wolves climb to fourth in the Championship with 28 points from 15 matches. His return from a loan spell at Celta Vigo has proved particularly valuable, with Wolves now targeting an immediate return to the Premier League.

Industry observers note that lopez’ return is a massive plus for Wolves, however they need to wary with him. The Spaniard has already picked up several knocks in this campaign, which will be a concern,.

Peixoto is clearly aware of the need to careful with him and will want to protect him this season. So far this campaign they have got away with him just picking up the odd short-term concern but if they keep persisting he will suffer a long-term problem, which would be a massive concern for Wolves this season.
